work.title: The Third Part of King Henry the Sixth
work.author: William Shakespeare

content.text: Enter King Edward, Richard (Duke of Gloucester), George (Duke of Clarence) and Lady Grey.

lines.text: Brother of Gloucester, at Saint Albans field
lines.plainText: Brother of Gloucester at Saint Albans field

lines.text: This lady's husband, Sir John Grey, was slain,
lines.plainText: This lady's husband Sir John Grey was slain

lines.text: His land then seized on by the conqueror.
lines.plainText: His land then seized on by the conqueror

lines.text: Her suit is now to repossess those lands,
lines.plainText: Her suit is now to repossess those lands

lines.text: Which we in justice cannot well deny,
lines.plainText: Which we in justice cannot well deny

lines.text: Because in quarrel of the house of York
lines.plainText: Because in quarrel of the house of York

lines.text: The worthy gentleman did lose his life.
lines.plainText: The worthy gentleman did lose his life

lines.text: Your Highness shall do well to grant her suit;
lines.plainText: Your Highness shall do well to grant her suit

lines.text: It were dishonour to deny it her.
lines.plainText: It were dishonour to deny it her

lines.text: It were no less; but yet I'll make a pause.
lines.plainText: It were no less but yet I'll make a pause

lines.text: [Aside to George.] Yea, is it so?
lines.plainText: Aside to George Yea is it so

lines.text: I see the lady hath a thing to grant
lines.plainText: I see the lady hath a thing to grant

lines.text: Before the King will grant her humble suit.
lines.plainText: Before the King will grant her humble suit

lines.text: [Aside to Richard.] He knows the game; how true he keeps the wind!
lines.plainText: Aside to Richard He knows the game how true he keeps the wind

lines.text: [Aside to George.] Silence!
lines.plainText: Aside to George Silence

lines.text: Widow, we will consider of your suit,
lines.plainText: Widow we will consider of your suit

lines.text: And come some other time to know our mind.
lines.plainText: And come some other time to know our mind

lines.text: Right gracious lord, I cannot brook delay.
lines.plainText: Right gracious lord I cannot brook delay

lines.text: May it please your Highness to resolve me now,
lines.plainText: May it please your Highness to resolve me now

lines.text: And what your pleasure is shall satisfy me.
lines.plainText: And what your pleasure is shall satisfy me

lines.text: [Aside to George.] Ay, widow? Then I'll warrant you all your lands,
lines.plainText: Aside to George Ay widow Then I'll warrant you all your lands

lines.text: An if what pleases him shall pleasure you.
lines.plainText: An if what pleases him shall pleasure you

lines.text: Fight closer, or, good faith, you'll catch a blow.
lines.plainText: Fight closer or good faith you'll catch a blow

lines.text: [Aside to Richard.] I fear her not, unless she chance to fall.
lines.plainText: Aside to Richard I fear her not unless she chance to fall

lines.text: [Aside to George.] God forbid that, for he'll take vantages.
lines.plainText: Aside to George God forbid that for he'll take vantages

lines.text: How many children hast thou, widow? Tell me.
lines.plainText: How many children hast thou widow Tell me

lines.text: [Aside to Richard.] I think he means to beg a child of her.
lines.plainText: Aside to Richard I think he means to beg a child of her

lines.text: [Aside to George.] Nay, whip me then; he'll rather give her two.
lines.plainText: Aside to George Nay whip me then he'll rather give her two

lines.text: Three, my most gracious lord.
lines.plainText: Three my most gracious lord

lines.text: [Aside to George.] You shall have four if you'll be ruled by him.
lines.plainText: Aside to George You shall have four if you'll be ruled by him

lines.text: 'Twere pity they should lose their father's lands.
lines.plainText: 'Twere pity they should lose their father's lands

lines.text: Be pitiful, dread lord, and grant it then.
lines.plainText: Be pitiful dread lord and grant it then

lines.text: Lords, give us leave; I'll try this widow's wit.
lines.plainText: Lords give us leave I'll try this widow's wit

lines.text: [Aside to George.] Ay, good leave have you; for you will have leave
lines.plainText: Aside to George Ay good leave have you for you will have leave

lines.text: Till youth take leave and leave you to the crutch.
lines.plainText: Till youth take leave and leave you to the crutch

lines.text: Now tell me, madam, do you love your children?
lines.plainText: Now tell me madam do you love your children

lines.text: Ay, full as dearly as I love myself.
lines.plainText: Ay full as dearly as I love myself

lines.text: And would you not do much to do them good?
lines.plainText: And would you not do much to do them good

lines.text: To do them good I would sustain some harm.
lines.plainText: To do them good I would sustain some harm

lines.text: Then get your husband's lands to do them good.
lines.plainText: Then get your husband's lands to do them good

lines.text: Therefore I came unto your majesty.
lines.plainText: Therefore I came unto your majesty

lines.text: I'll tell you how these lands are to be got.
lines.plainText: I'll tell you how these lands are to be got

lines.text: So shall you bind me to your Highness' service.
lines.plainText: So shall you bind me to your Highness' service

lines.text: What service wilt thou do me if I give them?
lines.plainText: What service wilt thou do me if I give them

lines.text: What you command that rests in me to do.
lines.plainText: What you command that rests in me to do

lines.text: But you will take exceptions to my boon.
lines.plainText: But you will take exceptions to my boon

lines.text: No, gracious lord, except I cannot do it.
lines.plainText: No gracious lord except I cannot do it

lines.text: Ay, but thou canst do what I mean to ask.
lines.plainText: Ay but thou canst do what I mean to ask

lines.text: Why, then, I will do what your Grace commands.
lines.plainText: Why then I will do what your Grace commands

lines.text: [Aside to George.] He plies her hard; and much rain wears the marble.
lines.plainText: Aside to George He plies her hard and much rain wears the marble

lines.text: [Aside to Richard.] As red as fire! Nay, then her wax must melt.
lines.plainText: Aside to Richard As red as fire Nay then her wax must melt

lines.text: Why stops my lord? Shall I not hear my task?
lines.plainText: Why stops my lord Shall I not hear my task

lines.text: An easy task; 'tis but to love a king.
lines.plainText: An easy task 'tis but to love a king

lines.text: That's soon performed, because I am a subject.
lines.plainText: That's soon performed because I am a subject

lines.text: Why, then, thy husband's lands I freely give thee.
lines.plainText: Why then thy husband's lands I freely give thee

lines.text: I take my leave with many thousand thanks.
lines.plainText: I take my leave with many thousand thanks

lines.text: [Aside to George.] The match is made; she seals it with a curtsy.
lines.plainText: Aside to George The match is made she seals it with a curtsy

lines.text: But stay thee; 'tis the fruits of love I mean.
lines.plainText: But stay thee 'tis the fruits of love I mean

lines.text: The fruits of love I mean, my loving liege.
lines.plainText: The fruits of love I mean my loving liege

lines.text: Ay, but, I fear me, in another sense.
lines.plainText: Ay but I fear me in another sense

lines.text: What love, thinkst thou, I sue so much to get?
lines.plainText: What love thinkst thou I sue so much to get

lines.text: My love till death, my humble thanks, my prayers;
lines.plainText: My love till death my humble thanks my prayers

lines.text: That love which virtue begs, and virtue grants.
lines.plainText: That love which virtue begs and virtue grants

lines.text: No, by my troth, I did not mean such love.
lines.plainText: No by my troth I did not mean such love

lines.text: Why, then, you mean not as I thought you did.
lines.plainText: Why then you mean not as I thought you did

lines.text: But now you partly may perceive my mind.
lines.plainText: But now you partly may perceive my mind

lines.text: My mind will never grant what I perceive
lines.plainText: My mind will never grant what I perceive

lines.text: Your Highness aims at, if I aim aright.
lines.plainText: Your Highness aims at if I aim aright

lines.text: To tell thee plain, I aim to lie with thee.
lines.plainText: To tell thee plain I aim to lie with thee

lines.text: To tell you plain, I had rather lie in prison.
lines.plainText: To tell you plain I had rather lie in prison

lines.text: Why, then thou shalt not have thy husband's lands.
lines.plainText: Why then thou shalt not have thy husband's lands

lines.text: Why, then mine honesty shall be my dower,
lines.plainText: Why then mine honesty shall be my dower

lines.text: For by that loss I will not purchase them.
lines.plainText: For by that loss I will not purchase them

lines.text: Therein thou wrong'st thy children mightily.
lines.plainText: Therein thou wrong'st thy children mightily

lines.text: Herein your Highness wrongs both them and me.
lines.plainText: Herein your Highness wrongs both them and me

lines.text: But, mighty lord, this merry inclination
lines.plainText: But mighty lord this merry inclination

lines.text: Accords not with the sadness of my suit.
lines.plainText: Accords not with the sadness of my suit

lines.text: Please you dismiss me either with ay or no.
lines.plainText: Please you dismiss me either with ay or no

lines.text: Ay, if thou wilt say ay to my request;
lines.plainText: Ay if thou wilt say ay to my request

lines.text: No, if thou dost say no to my demand.
lines.plainText: No if thou dost say no to my demand

lines.text: Then no, my lord. My suit is at an end.
lines.plainText: Then no my lord My suit is at an end

lines.text: [Aside to George.] The widow likes him not, she knits her brows.
lines.plainText: Aside to George The widow likes him not she knits her brows

lines.text: [Aside to Richard.] He is the bluntest wooer in Christendom.
lines.plainText: Aside to Richard He is the bluntest wooer in Christendom

lines.text: [Aside.] Her looks doth argue her replete with modesty;
lines.plainText: Aside Her looks doth argue her replete with modesty

lines.text: Her words doth show her wit incomparable;
lines.plainText: Her words doth show her wit incomparable

lines.text: All her perfections challenge sovereignty.
lines.plainText: All her perfections challenge sovereignty

lines.text: One way or other, she is for a king,
lines.plainText: One way or other she is for a king

lines.text: And she shall be my love, or else my queen.—
lines.plainText: And she shall be my love or else my queen

lines.text: Say that King Edward take thee for his queen?
lines.plainText: Say that King Edward take thee for his queen

lines.text: 'Tis better said than done, my gracious lord.
lines.plainText: 'Tis better said than done my gracious lord

lines.text: I am a subject fit to jest withal,
lines.plainText: I am a subject fit to jest withal

lines.text: But far unfit to be a sovereign.
lines.plainText: But far unfit to be a sovereign

lines.text: Sweet widow, by my state I swear to thee,
lines.plainText: Sweet widow by my state I swear to thee

lines.text: I speak no more than what my soul intends;
lines.plainText: I speak no more than what my soul intends

lines.text: And that is to enjoy thee for my love.
lines.plainText: And that is to enjoy thee for my love

lines.text: And that is more than I will yield unto.
lines.plainText: And that is more than I will yield unto

lines.text: I know I am too mean to be your queen,
lines.plainText: I know I am too mean to be your queen

lines.text: And yet too good to be your concubine.
lines.plainText: And yet too good to be your concubine

lines.text: You cavil, widow; I did mean my queen.
lines.plainText: You cavil widow I did mean my queen

lines.text: 'Twill grieve your Grace my sons should call you father.
lines.plainText: 'Twill grieve your Grace my sons should call you father

lines.text: No more than when my daughters call thee mother.
lines.plainText: No more than when my daughters call thee mother

lines.text: Thou art a widow, and thou hast some children;
lines.plainText: Thou art a widow and thou hast some children

lines.text: And, by God's mother, I, being but a bachelor,
lines.plainText: And by God's mother I being but a bachelor

lines.text: Have other some. Why, 'tis a happy thing
lines.plainText: Have other some Why 'tis a happy thing

lines.text: To be the father unto many sons.
lines.plainText: To be the father unto many sons

lines.text: Answer no more, for thou shalt be my queen.
lines.plainText: Answer no more for thou shalt be my queen

lines.text: [Aside to George.] The ghostly father now hath done his shrift.
lines.plainText: Aside to George The ghostly father now hath done his shrift

lines.text: [Aside to Richard.] When he was made a shriver, 'twas for shift.
lines.plainText: Aside to Richard When he was made a shriver 'twas for shift

lines.text: Brothers, you muse what chat we two have had.
lines.plainText: Brothers you muse what chat we two have had

lines.text: The widow likes it not, for she looks very sad.
lines.plainText: The widow likes it not for she looks very sad

lines.text: You'd think it strange if I should marry her.
lines.plainText: You'd think it strange if I should marry her

lines.text: To whom, my lord?
lines.plainText: To whom my lord

lines.text: Why, Clarence, to myself.
lines.plainText: Why Clarence to myself

lines.text: That would be ten days' wonder at the least.
lines.plainText: That would be ten days' wonder at the least

lines.text: That's a day longer than a wonder lasts.
lines.plainText: That's a day longer than a wonder lasts

lines.text: By so much is the wonder in extremes.
lines.plainText: By so much is the wonder in extremes

lines.text: Well, jest on, brothers. I can tell you both
lines.plainText: Well jest on brothers I can tell you both

lines.text: Her suit is granted for her husband's lands.
lines.plainText: Her suit is granted for her husband's lands

lines.text: My gracious lord, Henry your foe is taken,
lines.plainText: My gracious lord Henry your foe is taken

lines.text: And brought your prisoner to your palace gate.
lines.plainText: And brought your prisoner to your palace gate

lines.text: See that he be conveyed unto the Tower.
lines.plainText: See that he be conveyed unto the Tower

lines.text: And go we, brothers, to the man that took him,
lines.plainText: And go we brothers to the man that took him

lines.text: To question of his apprehension.
lines.plainText: To question of his apprehension

lines.text: Widow, go you along. Lords, use her honourably.
lines.plainText: Widow go you along Lords use her honourably

lines.text: Ay, Edward will use women honourably.
lines.plainText: Ay Edward will use women honourably

lines.text: Would he were wasted, marrow, bones, and all,
lines.plainText: Would he were wasted marrow bones and all

lines.text: That from his loins no hopeful branch may spring,
lines.plainText: That from his loins no hopeful branch may spring

lines.text: To cross me from the golden time I look for!
lines.plainText: To cross me from the golden time I look for

lines.text: And yet, between my soul's desire and me—
lines.plainText: And yet between my soul's desire and me

lines.text: The lustful Edward's title buried—
lines.plainText: The lustful Edward's title buried

lines.text: Is Clarence, Henry, and his son young Edward,
lines.plainText: Is Clarence Henry and his son young Edward

lines.text: And all the unlooked-for issue of their bodies,
lines.plainText: And all the unlookedfor issue of their bodies

lines.text: To take their rooms ere I can place myself.
lines.plainText: To take their rooms ere I can place myself

lines.text: A cold premeditation for my purpose!
lines.plainText: A cold premeditation for my purpose

lines.text: Why then I do but dream on sovereignty;
lines.plainText: Why then I do but dream on sovereignty

lines.text: Like one that stands upon a promontory
lines.plainText: Like one that stands upon a promontory

lines.text: And spies a far-off shore where he would tread,
lines.plainText: And spies a faroff shore where he would tread

lines.text: Wishing his foot were equal with his eye,
lines.plainText: Wishing his foot were equal with his eye

lines.text: And chides the sea that sunders him from thence,
lines.plainText: And chides the sea that sunders him from thence

lines.text: Saying he'll lade it dry to have his way.
lines.plainText: Saying he'll lade it dry to have his way

lines.text: So do I wish the crown, being so far off,
lines.plainText: So do I wish the crown being so far off

lines.text: And so I chide the means that keeps me from it;
lines.plainText: And so I chide the means that keeps me from it

lines.text: And so I say I'll cut the causes off,
lines.plainText: And so I say I'll cut the causes off

lines.text: Flattering me with impossibilities.
lines.plainText: Flattering me with impossibilities

lines.text: My eye's too quick, my heart o'erweens too much,
lines.plainText: My eye's too quick my heart o'erweens too much

lines.text: Unless my hand and strength could equal them.
lines.plainText: Unless my hand and strength could equal them

lines.text: Well, say there is no kingdom then for Richard,
lines.plainText: Well say there is no kingdom then for Richard

lines.text: What other pleasure can the world afford?
lines.plainText: What other pleasure can the world afford

lines.text: I'll make my heaven in a lady's lap,
lines.plainText: I'll make my heaven in a lady's lap

lines.text: And deck my body in gay ornaments,
lines.plainText: And deck my body in gay ornaments

lines.text: And 'witch sweet ladies with my words and looks.
lines.plainText: And 'witch sweet ladies with my words and looks

lines.text: O miserable thought, and more unlikely
lines.plainText: O miserable thought and more unlikely

lines.text: Than to accomplish twenty golden crowns.
lines.plainText: Than to accomplish twenty golden crowns

lines.text: Why, Love forswore me in my mother's womb,
lines.plainText: Why Love forswore me in my mother's womb

lines.text: And, for I should not deal in her soft laws,
lines.plainText: And for I should not deal in her soft laws

lines.text: She did corrupt frail Nature with some bribe
lines.plainText: She did corrupt frail Nature with some bribe

lines.text: To shrink mine arm up like a withered shrub;
lines.plainText: To shrink mine arm up like a withered shrub

lines.text: To make an envious mountain on my back,
lines.plainText: To make an envious mountain on my back

lines.text: Where sits Deformity to mock my body;
lines.plainText: Where sits Deformity to mock my body

lines.text: To shape my legs of an unequal size;
lines.plainText: To shape my legs of an unequal size

lines.text: To disproportion me in every part,
lines.plainText: To disproportion me in every part

lines.text: Like to a chaos, or an unlicked bear-whelp
lines.plainText: Like to a chaos or an unlicked bearwhelp

lines.text: That carries no impression like the dam.
lines.plainText: That carries no impression like the dam

lines.text: And am I then a man to be beloved?
lines.plainText: And am I then a man to be beloved

lines.text: O monstrous fault to harbour such a thought!
lines.plainText: O monstrous fault to harbour such a thought

lines.text: Then, since this earth affords no joy to me
lines.plainText: Then since this earth affords no joy to me

lines.text: But to command, to check, to o'erbear such
lines.plainText: But to command to check to o'erbear such

lines.text: As are of better person than myself,
lines.plainText: As are of better person than myself

lines.text: I'll make my heaven to dream upon the crown,
lines.plainText: I'll make my heaven to dream upon the crown

lines.text: And, whiles I live, t' account this world but hell
lines.plainText: And whiles I live t' account this world but hell

lines.text: Until my misshaped trunk that bear this head
lines.plainText: Until my misshaped trunk that bear this head

lines.text: Be round impaled with a glorious crown.
lines.plainText: Be round impaled with a glorious crown

lines.text: And yet I know not how to get the crown,
lines.plainText: And yet I know not how to get the crown

lines.text: For many lives stand between me and home;
lines.plainText: For many lives stand between me and home

lines.text: And I, like one lost in a thorny wood,
lines.plainText: And I like one lost in a thorny wood

lines.text: That rents the thorns, and is rent with the thorns,
lines.plainText: That rents the thorns and is rent with the thorns

lines.text: Seeking a way, and straying from the way,
lines.plainText: Seeking a way and straying from the way

lines.text: Not knowing how to find the open air,
lines.plainText: Not knowing how to find the open air

lines.text: But toiling desperately to find it out,
lines.plainText: But toiling desperately to find it out

lines.text: Torment myself to catch the English crown.
lines.plainText: Torment myself to catch the English crown

lines.text: And from that torment I will free myself,
lines.plainText: And from that torment I will free myself

lines.text: Or hew my way out with a bloody axe.
lines.plainText: Or hew my way out with a bloody axe

lines.text: Why, I can smile, and murder while I smile,
lines.plainText: Why I can smile and murder while I smile

lines.text: And cry "Content!" to that which grieves my heart,
lines.plainText: And cry Content to that which grieves my heart

lines.text: And wet my cheeks with artificial tears,
lines.plainText: And wet my cheeks with artificial tears

lines.text: And frame my face to all occasions.
lines.plainText: And frame my face to all occasions

lines.text: I'll drown more sailors than the mermaid shall,
lines.plainText: I'll drown more sailors than the mermaid shall

lines.text: I'll slay more gazers than the basilisk;
lines.plainText: I'll slay more gazers than the basilisk

lines.text: I'll play the orator as well as Nestor,
lines.plainText: I'll play the orator as well as Nestor

lines.text: Deceive more slyly than Ulysses could,
lines.plainText: Deceive more slyly than Ulysses could

lines.text: And, like a Sinon, take another Troy.
lines.plainText: And like a Sinon take another Troy

lines.text: I can add colours to the chameleon,
lines.plainText: I can add colours to the chameleon

lines.text: Change shapes with Proteus for advantages,
lines.plainText: Change shapes with Proteus for advantages

lines.text: And set the murderous Machiavel to school.
lines.plainText: And set the murderous Machiavel to school

lines.text: Can I do this, and cannot get a crown?
lines.plainText: Can I do this and cannot get a crown

lines.text: Tut, were it farther off, I'll pluck it down.
lines.plainText: Tut were it farther off I'll pluck it down
